item: BackgroundScheduler.start() records a start only when the loop thread exists
summary: start() stamped started_at and stored the new thread before Thread.start(); when the process was out of threads (RuntimeError can't start new thread) status() reported a start that never happened and the scheduler held a never-started thread. Both are now recorded once the OS thread exists, also when start() raises after it exists (the live loop must not be started twice). Found in the read of #1638 as cosmetic.
